evidence.quote: Bachelor's Programme in Software and Systems Engineering, Bachelor's thesis 2026
Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools have become a regular part of software development.

Six developers at various seniority levels from different organisations in Northern Europe were interviewed between December 2025 and July 2026. The semi-structured interviews were analysed using thematic analysis, guided by the SPACE framework for developer productivity.
Figure 4 shows how the findings map onto the five dimensions, and the following paragraphs go through them one by one.
Overall, participants reported productivity improvements, although the estimated magnitude varied considerably across individuals and development tasks.

The studies reviewed in Chapter two report a 55.8% speed-up (Peng et al., 2023), a 19% slowdown (Becker et al., 2025), and a 26.08% increase in completed tasks (Cui et al., 2025). This chapter argues that the two observations are connected.
The effect on satisfaction and well-being was mixed rather than entirely positive. GenAI reduced the amount of manual work, but it did not remove uncertainty or the effort of checking the output.

What did change was the focus of collaboration. As the tools took over code-level checking in pull requests, discussion moved away from individual lines of code and towards architecture, requirements and system design.

This study did not collect repository-level activity metrics. Nevertheless, the interviews suggest that common activity measures, such as lines of code or commits, tend to capture code generation only.
